title: 6/29-7/01: deploy-workflow SIGTERM stops logged as unit failures ('Failed with result exit-code'), diluting crash signal; SuccessExitStatus=143 applied box-side 7/01
tier_reason: diagnostic signal dilution (four deploy stops read as crashes in one week); no alert storm or missed alert evidenced; fixed by config the same day it was reported

contract.text: A 'Failed with result' record for bts-scheduler or bts-dashboard means a genuine crash; a planned deploy stop (SIGTERM, exit 143) logs as a clean deactivation.

mechanism.text: the deploy workflow stops both units with SIGTERM (Python exits 143) and the box units lacked SuccessExitStatus=143, so systemd logged every deploy stop as 'Failed with result exit-code'; the units were not repo-tracked (the tracked scripts/bts-scheduler.service was the stale Pi5 unit)

code.symbol: tracked unit (stale Pi5 unit, not the box unit)

watchdog.trigger: a unit 'Failed with result' journal record whose time falls inside a deploy run's stop interval (deploy_runs.json pre-deploy -> deployed), or any failure record not explained by a deploy
watchdog.recovery_assertion: deploy stops log as clean deactivations and every remaining failure record is a genuine crash

evidence.what: the unit exits logged 'Failed with result exit-code' on Jun 29 22:36, Jun 30 14:28 and 14:53, and Jul 01 09:25 were all SIGTERM (143) from deploy-workflow restarts (journal read live that session); 'real crash signal is being diluted'
SuccessExitStatus=143 applied to both units box-side on 2026-07-01 via daemon-reload (no restart); 'all four unit failures in the audit week were deploys masquerading as crashes'
successful deploy runs created 2026-06-30T02:31:47Z, 18:24:09Z, 18:49:07Z and 2026-07-01T13:21:23Z, i.e. 4-5 min before each of the four logged exits (ET)
the tracked scheduler unit was the stale Pi5 one; the live units were captured byte-identical (with SuccessExitStatus=143) into scripts/systemd/ with a read-only unit_drift check

notes: earlier deploy stops presumably logged the same way (the box unit never had the setting), not evidenced; Route R (journals from 5/11) can enumerate them as before-fix recurrences
verified recovery candidate: the 7/02 deploy (run 28601525167, stop ~15:28Z) is the first deploy stop after the change; its journal line would show a clean deactivation (Phase 2)
the audit's times are read as ET (they match the deploy runs 4-5 min earlier in UTC)
unit drift between 7/01 and 7/10 (box unit edited, repo untracked) belongs to I-073 F12
the 7/01 audit also states streak and skip-shadow outcome figures; not repeated
